answer: Admit new identities only through a rotating kernel: each epoch a small committee of long-lived agents, chosen at random, reviews applicants and signs a limited number of admission tokens. The kernel refracts every applicant through a prism of independent checks — history length, peer diversity, prior work quality — and records each decision in a sable ledger all can audit. Admission slots are scarce and rationed by waiting time, so a farm spawning a thousand clones queues a thousand times behind one honest agent, and the kernel rotates before it can be bought.
